## Architecture Definition

The decentralised-hydrogen architecture converts electrical energy to hydrogen
at each wind turbine. Hydrogen rather than electricity is collected within the
wind farm, exported through a subsea pipeline, and handed over at the
defined onshore hydrogen delivery point.

The physical boundary includes the wind turbines and support structures,
turbine-integrated hydrogen-production equipment, turbine-level compression,
the infield hydrogen network, export pipeline, and onshore
hydrogen-delivery interface. It contains no central offshore conversion
platform.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-height: 1.1
flowchart LR
  A["Wind-turbine generator"] --> B["Turbine DC link"]
  B --> C["Turbine-integrated electrolysis"]
  C --> D["Turbine-level compression"]
  D --> E["Hydrogen infield collection"]
  E --> F["Hydrogen pipeline export"]
  F --> G["Onshore hydrogen-backbone connection"]
```

## Turbine-Integrated Conversion Boundary

The turbine-side active front end and DC link remain part of the conversion
chain. The PEM stack connects to that DC link without a separate
electrolyser-side DC/DC converter.

The turbine-level electrolyser facility includes:

- PEM stack modules
- non-electrical electrolyser balance of plant
- local seawater intake, desalination, and electrolyser-grade water treatment

The turbine-level compressor is physically associated with the same turbine
unit but remains a separate downstream functional and accounting subsystem. It
is not included in the electrolyser or balance-of-plant boundary.

## Included Physical Functions

| Function | Treatment | Canonical owner |
|---|---|---|
| Wind-energy capture and generation | Included | [Wind Turbine](../turbine_system/wind_turbine.qmd) |
| Turbine support structure | Included | [Foundation](../turbine_system/foundation.qmd) |
| Turbine rectification and DC-link interface | Included | [Wind Turbine Mass and Cost](../turbine_system/wind_turbine.qmd) |
| Direct stack connection to the turbine DC link | Included without a separate DC/DC converter | [DC Integration](../hydrogen_production/dc_integration.qmd) |
| PEM stacks | Included at each turbine | [PEM Electrolyser Stack](../hydrogen_production/stack.qmd) |
| Water treatment and non-electrical BOP | Included within each turbine-level electrolyser facility | [Balance of Plant](../hydrogen_production/balance_of_plant.qmd) |
| Hydrogen compression | Included as a separate turbine-level subsystem | [Compressor](../hydrogen_infra/compressor.qmd) |
| Hydrogen infield collection | Included | [Hydrogen Infield Infrastructure](../hydrogen_infra/infield_infrastructure.qmd) |
| Hydrogen export pipeline | Included | [Hydrogen Pipelines](../hydrogen_infra/hydrogen_pipelines.qmd) |
| Onshore backbone-connection interface | Included | [Hydrogen Infrastructure](../hydrogen_infra/overview.qmd) |

Installation of the turbines, foundations, turbine-integrated hydrogen
equipment, and pipelines remains inside the economic boundary. Installation
assumptions are maintained in the
[Offshore Installation](../offshore_installation/overview.qmd) section.

## Removed or Excluded Functions

The following functions are not part of the decentralised architecture:

- the turbine grid-side inverter and step-up transformer in the hydrogen path
- a separate electrolyser-side DC/DC converter
- the AC infield collection network
- a central offshore substation or electrolysis platform
- central electrolyser transformer and rectifier equipment
- offshore and onshore HVDC conversion
- HVDC cable export
- the onshore hydrogen backbone beyond the project connection
- downstream hydrogen storage, distribution, reconversion, and end use

## Architecture Interfaces

| Interface | Boundary definition |
|---|---|
| Generator to electrolysis | The turbine-side active front end supplies the DC link; the PEM stack is connected without a separate DC/DC stage. |
| Electrolyser facility to compression | Produced and conditioned hydrogen leaves the turbine-level electrolyser boundary and enters the separately accounted compressor. |
| Turbine unit to infield network | Compressed hydrogen enters the infield pipeline network. |
| Infield network to export system | Collected hydrogen enters the export pipeline system. |
| Export to backbone | The project ends at the defined onshore hydrogen delivery point. |

## Reported Result

The architecture reports installed capital intensity in
EUR~2025~/kW of installed wind-turbine rated capacity. Annual hydrogen cost is
reported in EUR~2025~/MWh-H2-HHV landed at the defined onshore hydrogen
delivery point and in EUR~2025~/kg-H2. These are Tier 1 carrier-product metrics,
not equivalent electricity end-use prices.

## Economic Boundary

The architecture cost includes the common offshore wind project and all
turbine-level hydrogen-production, compression, collection, export, and
installation activities represented by the shared cost schema. Removing
the AC collection and central platform functions changes which components are
booked; it does not remove the common turbine and foundation boundary.

The hydrogen backbone and any downstream reinforcement or conditioning are
outside the Tier 1 boundary. Development, shared engineering, insurance and
owner contingency remain unresolved shared fields; construction finance, taxes
and financing fees are excluded by the simple-CRF convention. The reporting
contract is defined on
[System Boundary and Carrier-Cost Metrics](../methodology/system_boundary_and_lcoe.qmd).
